record.original_question: Let zeta(s) denote the Riemann zeta function. Do all nontrivial zeros of zeta(s) have real part equal to 1/2?

evidence.quote: The Riemann zeta function is a complex function defined for Re(s)>1 by ζ(s)=sum over n of 1/n^s and analytically extended elsewhere.
Riemann hypothesis. The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) have real part equal to 1/2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the Riemann zeta function for complex s with Re(s) > 1 by the absolutely convergent series ζ(s) = Σ_{n=1}^∞ 1/n^s, and extend it by analytic continuation to a meromorphic function on the whole complex plane, whose only singularity is a simple pole at s = 1. The functional equation implies that ζ(s) vanishes at the negative even integers s = -2, -4, -6, …; these are called the trivial zeros. All other zeros of ζ(s) are called nontrivial zeros and are known to lie in the critical strip 0 < Re(s) < 1.

Prove or disprove: every nontrivial zero ρ of ζ(s) satisfies Re(ρ) = 1/2.
